MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  January 12, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:00 p.m., on January 12, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on January 8, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:04 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:00 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

CLOSED SESSION

City Council Minutes  1  January 12, 2016
 CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Anticipated Litigation. Significant Exposure to
  Litigation Pursuant to Paragraph (2) or (3) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9. (5
  potential cases): Funding/Site Remediation Issues Related to Slope Failure Issues.

CS2. Public Employee Performance Evaluation of the Incumbent for the Position of City
  Manager Pursuant to Government Code Sections 54957 and 54957.6.

CS3. Conference With Legal Counsel: Consideration of Initiation of Litigation Pursuant
  to Paragraph (4) of Subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: One Case; Adverse to State of
  California.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that CS1 involved a potential litigation matter. The Council gave
direction to staff but no reportable action occurred. CS2 was a personnel matter and the Council
gave direction and will continue the evaluation of the City Manager in the future. CS3 was
consideration of litigation. The City Council unanimously gave direction for staff to commence
litigation against the State Department of Finance.

INVOCATION: Council Member Raths

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

 12.  Fiscal Year 2015-16 Mission Viejo Housing Authority Annual Report

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  Council Member Schlicht inquired about the homeownership unit losses to the Housing
  Successor’s portfolio (on the last page of the report) which lists one unit with an $11,500
  loss.

  Director Dyas responded that this was a home rehabilitation loan and the house was sold
  under short sale. The City tried to negotiate as much as they could to repay the entire loan
  balance but there was a loss due to lack of equity as noted in the report.

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to
  receive and file.

City Council Minutes  10  January 12, 2016
 Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths said that he had nothing to report.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he has asked the City Manager to begin to supply the City
Council with monthly status reports on the Aquatics Center rehabilitation progress. He noted that
the City did a wonderful job of repaving his neighborhood but Santa Margarita Water District
came through afterwards and messed the street up. He said that the City’s work has been undone
and he hopes that the Water District will find a color match for the pavement and repair the
problem. Council Member Sachs stated that when he read through the annual CAFR, he noticed
that the gap is closing between the growth of the City’s expenses and its income over the last ten
years. Tax revenues were only up about 2% since 2009 and expenses continue to grow. Council
Member Sachs said that the CalPERS portfolio growth estimation is continually wrong and
taxpayers will have to make that up. There will be increased pension liabilities and there is
geopolitical unrest and market volatility. Council Member Sachs stated that it would be in the best
interest of the Council and staff to begin working on implementing a reduction of expenses of 5%
per year for the next five years and he said he will sit down with staff and Mayor Ury to see what
can be done.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht asked staff about three median lights that were down on Alicia and
Marguerite over the last couple of weeks and if that was due to the rain storm. She also asked if
there is an update on possible animal services expansion in the cities of Laguna Hills and Rancho
Santa Margarita. She said she is very concerned about the PACE program and the negative effects
it can have. She noted that Orange County Treasurer-Tax Collector Sherry Friedenrich has created
an overview of PACE which gives some very good buyer-beware recommendations. Council
Member Schlicht congratulated the Mission Viejo High School Diablos football team on their
recent winning streak. She thanked Mayor Ury for his kind comments regarding her term as Mayor
and stated that 2015 proved her belief that reasonable minds can disagree and work together. She
thanked the residents of Mission Viejo for their warm reception wherever she was and stated that
she is looking forward to the work ahead this year as the Council continues on its path of serving.
Council Member Schlicht thanked her family, her boss, and her friends for their support and she
also thanked the Commissioners who understood their role to advise the Council and not be rubber
stamps. She expressed thanks for her colleagues’ support in fulfilling her promise to residents to
change the direction of the City. She discussed her hopes for the New Year and again, cautioned
residents against PACE loans. Council Member Schlicht thanked Lt. NewMyer and the Orange
County Sheriff’s Department for their dedication to residents’ safety and she concluded with a
quote from Samuel Adams: “The Constitution shall never be construed to prevent the people of
the United States, who are peaceable citizens, from keeping their own arms.”

City Council Minutes  11  January 12, 2016
 Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum commended the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce for a great
holiday event. She also outlined her attendance at other recent events including the Association
of California Cities-Orange County (ACC-OC) Board of Directors elections and the ACC-OC,
Orange County Business Council and Building Industry Association joint holiday reception.
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum said that she is excited about the path that has been set by Mayor Ury
to focus on economic development and technology and she thanked staff for looking into electronic
building permits and the availability of sports fields and room rentals online. She also said that she
looks forward to upgrading the Marguerite Aquatics Center and she feels that the timing is perfect
after the receipt of park development fees so the City doesn’t have to use tax dollars. Mayor Pro
Tem Bucknum shared her kudos for the Diablos football team and announced that they will be
recognized at the next Council Meeting with a procession from the high school up La Paz Road to
City Hall. She encouraged residents to stand out and cheer the buses as they come up the road.
Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum stated that she is excited to work with Mayor Ury. She has known him
for many years and she had no idea that one day she would be serving on the City Council with
him. She stated that it is an honor to serve as Mayor Pro Tem under Mayor Ury and she looks
forward to being of service to the community. Lastly, she asked if Lt. NewMyer or his
representative can do a presentation on safety and how to be aware of ones surroundings as a
follow-up to the recent terrorist activities in San Bernardino.

Mayor Ury

Mayor Ury thanked his colleagues for their very gracious comments. He said he appreciates the
opportunity to serve, once again as Mayor. He stated that the Council’s hard work last year created
the prelude for this year and there will be a lot of good accomplishments in 2016. Mayor Ury
expressed his hope that everyone recharged over the holidays and spent quality time with family
and friends and he said he is looking forward to good year ahead.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:51 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ury adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, January 26, 2016, at 5:00 p.m.
